# Inventory Structure

This document defines the proposed inventory domain, REST endpoints, and stock
movement rules for this ERP project. It follows the module layout and
controller/service/route separation described in
[file_tree_structure.md](./file_tree_structure.md), and the authentication,
authorization, validation, and paginated-list conventions described in
[users_roles_permissions.md](./users_roles_permissions.md).

Inventory modules are not implemented yet. Treat the paths and behaviors below
as the target specification, not as a description of existing endpoints.

## Shared conventions

- API paths are rooted at `/api` and use explicit plural, kebab-case resource
  names as listed below. The current server derives paths by converting a module
  folder name to kebab case and appending `s`; this does not correctly handle
  every plural (for example, `category` becomes `categorys`). Update route
  mounting to support the canonical paths rather than changing these API names.
- Each resource is a self-contained module under `server/modules/`, following
  the existing `Model`, `Validations`, `Service`, `Controller`, and `Routes`
  pattern where applicable.
- All endpoints require authentication except where explicitly stated.
  Protect each operation with `authorize(route, access)` and validate request
  input at the route boundary, following the existing users and roles modules.
- List endpoints use the existing pagination shape:
  `{ items, total, page, limit }`. Default to 10 results and cap the requested
  limit at 100; support search where useful.
- Documents have a database ID and a unique human-readable document number
  (for example, `PR-000001`). Document numbers are generated by the server and
  are not client-supplied identifiers.
- Quantities on transaction lines must be positive. Adjustment lines also
  record an explicit direction (`increase` or `decrease`); do not encode
  direction with signed quantities.
- Use the stock's base unit of measure for inventory balances. If transactions
  allow a different unit, store the conversion used so historical quantities
  remain interpretable.

## Master data

Master-data records support the standard authenticated list, create, read,
update, and delete operations. Do not physically delete a record referenced by
an inventory document; reject the deletion or use the project's established
soft-delete pattern.

| Resource | Endpoint | Purpose and key relationships |
|---|---|---|
| Stocks | `/api/stocks` | Items held in inventory. Include a unique SKU, name, description, category, base unit of measure, and reorder level. An optional default supplier may be recorded. Customers are related to sales documents, not directly to stock. |
| Suppliers | `/api/suppliers` | Supplier name, address, and contact information. Referenced by purchase orders and receiving documents. |
| Customers | `/api/customers` | Customer name, address, and contact information. Referenced by sales orders and delivery receipts. |
| Units of Measure | `/api/unit-of-measures` | Unique unit name/code and description. Referenced by stocks and, where applicable, transaction lines. |
| Categories | `/api/categories` | Unique category name and description. Referenced by stocks. |
| Warehouses | `/api/warehouses` | Unique warehouse name/code, address, and contact information. Referenced by receiving, delivery, transfers, adjustments, counts, and stock balances. |

The stock reorder level is a threshold, not a stock movement. This
specification treats it as a per-stock threshold; if reorder planning needs to
vary by warehouse, model the threshold per stock/warehouse instead.

## Transactions

Transaction documents contain one or more lines. Each line references a stock
and records quantity in the stock's base unit (or records the transaction unit
and conversion as described above). Documents also include their number,
status, relevant party/warehouse references, dates, and timestamps.

| Resource | Endpoint | Purpose and relationships |
|---|---|---|
| Purchase Requests | `/api/purchase-requests` | Internal request to procure stock. Has a unique PR number and stock/quantity lines. A request may be converted to one or more purchase orders; it need not name a supplier before sourcing. |
| Purchase Orders | `/api/purchase-orders` | Supplier order with a unique PO number, supplier, and stock/quantity lines. May reference the purchase request(s) it fulfills. |
| Stocks Receiving | `/api/stocks-receiving` | Inbound receipt with a unique SR number, source purchase order, supplier, destination warehouse, and received stock/quantity lines. Posting adds the received quantities to inventory. |
| Sales Orders | `/api/sales-orders` | Customer order with a unique SO number, customer, and stock/quantity lines. Provides the correct source document for outbound deliveries. |
| Delivery Receipts | `/api/delivery-receipts` | Outbound delivery with a unique DR number, sales order, customer, source warehouse, and delivered stock/quantity lines. Posting deducts delivered quantities from inventory. |
| Stocks Transfers | `/api/stocks-transfers` | Inter-warehouse transfer with a unique ST number, source warehouse, destination warehouse, and stock/quantity lines. Posting deducts from the source and adds the same quantities to the destination. |
| Inventory Adjustments | `/api/inventory-adjustments` | Controlled correction with a unique IA number, warehouse, reason, and stock/quantity lines. Posting changes inventory by the recorded adjustment quantities. |
| Physical Counts | `/api/physical-counts` | Count session with a unique PC number, warehouse, and stock lines. Record the system quantity at count start, the counted quantity, and the variance. Finalizing a count must reconcile the variance through an inventory adjustment or an equivalent auditable stock movement. |

### Transaction lifecycle and inventory effects

- Create documents as drafts. Drafts and submitted/approved documents do not
  change on-hand stock.
- Only posting a receiving document, delivery receipt, transfer, or inventory
  adjustment changes on-hand stock. A transfer posts both warehouse effects
  together; it must not leave stock removed from one warehouse but not added to
  the other.
- Posting records an auditable stock movement with the source document,
  warehouse, stock, quantity, and timestamp. On-hand balances must be
  attributable to these movements.
- A posted document is immutable and cannot be deleted. Correct a posted
  transaction with a reversing/correction document that preserves the audit
  trail. Drafts may be edited or deleted; cancellation of an unposted document
  must not change stock.
- Approval requirements may differ by document type, but approval and posting
  must be distinct from editing. Define any required approval permissions before
  implementing a workflow.
- Reject a posting that would result in negative stock unless an explicit,
  documented business policy permits it.
- A purchase order is inbound procurement and must not be used as the source
  for a customer delivery. Customer deliveries reference sales orders.

## API operations

- **Master data:** list, create, read, update, and delete subject to the
  reference/soft-delete rules above.
- **Transactions:** list, create, and read; update or delete drafts only;
  provide explicit submit/approve/post/cancel actions as required by each
  workflow. Posted documents use reversal/correction rather than update or
  delete.
- For list filters, support relevant fields such as status, document number,
  supplier/customer, warehouse, stock, and date range. Do not return an
  unbounded result set.

## Module mapping

Use the canonical endpoint paths in this document when mounting inventory
routes. For example:

| Module folder | Mounted endpoint |
|---|---|
| `stock` | `/api/stocks` |
| `supplier` | `/api/suppliers` |
| `customer` | `/api/customers` |
| `unitOfMeasure` | `/api/unit-of-measures` |
| `category` | `/api/categories` |
| `warehouse` | `/api/warehouses` |
| `purchaseRequest` | `/api/purchase-requests` |
| `purchaseOrder` | `/api/purchase-orders` |
| `stockReceiving` | `/api/stocks-receiving` |
| `salesOrder` | `/api/sales-orders` |
| `deliveryReceipt` | `/api/delivery-receipts` |
| `stockTransfer` | `/api/stocks-transfers` |
| `inventoryAdjustment` | `/api/inventory-adjustments` |
| `physicalCount` | `/api/physical-counts` |

These mappings are explicit because simply appending `s` to a converted module
folder name does not produce all of the required endpoint plurals.
